```{python}
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "part06"))
from cafe_clean import clean_sales

sales, log = clean_sales()
sales = sales.assign(monto=sales["monto"].astype(float))
if category != "all":
    sales = sales[sales["categoria"] == category]

total = sales["monto"].sum()
count = len(sales)
scope = "all categories" if category == "all" else f"the category {category}"
```

## Summary

This report covers `{python} scope`. In January 2024 Café Central made
`{python} f"{count:,}"` sales for a total of `{python} f"{total:,.0f}"` colones.

## Sales by week

```{python}
#| label: fig-weekly
#| fig-cap: "Weekly sales in colones."
weekly = sales.set_index("fecha")["monto"].resample("W-SUN").sum()
figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
axis.bar([d.strftime("%d %b") for d in weekly.index], weekly.values, color="#4F6D7A")
axis.set_ylim(0, None)
axis.set_ylabel("Colones")
axis.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

@fig-weekly shows the weekly totals. The axis starts at zero.

## Sales by category

```{python}
by_category = sales.groupby("categoria")["monto"].agg(["count", "sum"])
lines = ["| Category | Sales | Total (colones) |", "| --- | ---: | ---: |"]
lines += [f"| {name} | {row['count']:.0f} | {row['sum']:,.0f} |" for name, row in by_category.iterrows()]
Markdown("\n".join(lines))
```
